name: Radial band split on an unshifted FFT (bands swapped)
plain: Two nodes build a radial mask centred at (h/2, w/2) and multiply it onto an FFT that was never fftshift-ed. In an unshifted FFT, DC sits at the corner and the centre holds the highest frequencies. So the output labelled low or macro holds the highest frequencies and DC lands in the high or micro band. Recombining all bands still looks fine, which hides this.
math:
F=fft2(x) with no shift; d=‖(y,x)−(h/2,w/2)‖/max
Jurdn: low=σ((le−d)/o·10), mid=σ((d−le+o)/o·10)·σ((me−d)/o·10), high=σ((d−me+o)/o·10)
masks do not sum to 1
Omni: hard bands at macro_cutoff, mid_cutoff; recombine sum or weighted
band=ifft2(F·mask).real

props.params: low_freq_end, mid_freq_end, overlap; macro_cutoff=.2, mid_cutoff=.6, recombination

label: from code
surprise: freqsep.py:25 and latent_frequency_band_splitter.py:49 mask an unshifted FFT with a centre-based radius, so "low" and "high" bands are inverted. Reasoned from code, not run.
